Independent exact small-field commutator rank and commuting-pair counts
correctness.rationale: The arrow rows of [x,y] are δ_i v_i−u_i(c_i−c_{i+1}), with δ_i=d_i−d_{i+1}. A nonzero δ_i gives its own pivot, independent of the remaining incidence rows. Any proper subset of cycle incidence rows is independent by leaf elimination; the full set has rank n−1, also for the opposed arrows at n=2 and in characteristic two. The provisional rank counts the number of positions with either δ_i or u_i nonzero. Only constant diagonals with all u_i nonzero need correction down by one, giving q(q−1)^n(z^{n−1}−z^n). As an independent count of the provisional part, each zero-sum δ-vector has q diagonal preimages, and the number of zero-sum ordered lists of s nonzero differences is A_s=((q−1)^s+(q−1)(−1)^s)/q, by A_0=1 and A_{s+1}=(q−1)^s−A_s. Summing q binom(n,s) A_s (qz)^s[1+(q−1)z]^{n−s} gives the first two terms of P. The rank zero elements are scalar diagonals with no arrows; every k<n is realized by constant diagonal and k nonzero arrow coordinates, and rank n by nonconstant diagonal and nonzero arrows at all equal-diagonal edges. The probability is q^{−2n}P(q^{−1}). Independently, one can count commuting pairs by treating the pair of diagonal entries at each vertex as one of q² joint labels: each arrow permits q² choices for its two coefficients on equal labels and q on unequal labels. The cycle trace with these weights gives the same probability. Direct bounded counts gave 7/16 for (q,n)=(2,2), 1/4 for (2,3), and 17/81 for (3,2); separate full commutator-matrix checks gave the respective rank histograms (2,6,8), (2,6,32,24), and (3,24,54).
residual_risks: Proof applies to exactly one arrow per cyclic step, including the two distinct opposed arrows at n=2. The uploaded checker was not executed.

evidence: In the October 12 formula, Z is the equal-label edge set and S the nonzero arrow support within Z; the rank exponent is n−|Z|+r(S) on a cycle. The only S with r(S)≠|S| is S=E, requiring Z=E. Its coefficient is the q constant labels times (q−1)^n and it shifts from exponent n to n−1.

Replacing r(S) by |S| yields cycle weights U=1+(q−1)z for equal labels and V=qz for unequal labels. The transfer trace is [U+(q−1)V]^n+(q−1)(U−V)^n, exactly the frozen first two terms. Evaluating at 1/q and normalizing gives the probability.

For n=2 the earlier same-direction product has two commutator coordinates of the form (d_0−d_1)v_i−u_i(c_0−c_1). The frozen opposed second arrow has the negative of this second coordinate, an invertible output change for all q.

originality.rationale: The already catalogued October 12 graphic-matroid rank enumerator applies to every consistently oriented simple cycle n≥3. Its specialization gives the entire claimed polynomial, including the top-rank correction. The excluded n=2 case has the same commutator pencil ranks as the October 4 two-arrow Kronecker example by an explicit invertible sign change on the commutator output; it does not supply a distinct surviving invariant.
residual_risks: No exhaustive scholarly priority claim. Some broader searches were deferred and the Baclawski incidence-algebra derivations full text was unavailable. The rejection rests on exact inspected formula-level overlap and explicit implications, not on any unavailable literature.

value.rationale: The full rank spectrum is a useful invariant of a natural family and the cycle dependence provides a clean example, but the supported contribution is a routine special case of the existing general enumerator, with the exceptional two-vertex case having an already computed commutator-equivalent spectrum. Re-presenting the specialization is not a surviving scientific advance.
residual_risks: This does not judge the value of a theorem for other radical lengths or for finer invariants not computed in the frozen record.
